definitions.explanation: To send something (a letter, message, goods) to the speaker. Implies the item is coming toward the speaker.
To give or pass something to the speaker, sometimes used as a demand.

examples.japanese: {友人|ゆうじん}がメールを{寄越|よこ}した。
examples.english: A friend sent me an email.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}が{田舎|いなか}から{野菜|やさい}を{寄越|よこ}してくれた。
examples.english: My mother sent me vegetables from the countryside.

examples.japanese: {金|かね}を{寄越|よこ}せと{言|い}われた。
examples.english: I was told to hand over the money.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が「おやつ{寄越|よこ}せ」と{騒|さわ}いでいる。
examples.english: The kids are clamoring, "Give us snacks!"

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). Pattern: Xを{寄越|よこ}す.

USAGE:
This verb describes things or people being sent toward the speaker. The imperative form {寄越|よこ}せ is commonly used as a blunt demand. The verb always implies movement toward the speaker's location or benefit.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{手紙|てがみ}を{寄越|よこ}す (to send a letter)
・{返事|へんじ}を{寄越|よこ}す (to send a reply)
・{人|ひと}を{寄越|よこ}す (to send someone over)
・{寄越|よこ}せ (hand it over — imperative)
